# sumhut — complete product guide

Updated: 2026-10-18
Canonical website: https://sumhut.com/
Default language: English
Documentation language order: English, Spanish, Portuguese, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese.
The website offers 30 interface languages. This five-language documentation set does not describe the total interface language count.

## Capabilities
Search food or everyday objects, adjust quantity or source portions, estimate mass in g/kg, available volume in mL/L and weight force in N, inspect calories and nutrients, build combination lists, export CSV and share calculation URLs. Selected Foundation/FNDDS food records expose reported vitamins and minerals. Not every item contains every nutrient. Community supports posts and media, plus account-based messaging. iPhone users can add the site to their Home Screen.

## Calculation rules
Mass and weight force differ. Weight force = mass in kg × 9.80665 m/s². Volume is available only when supported by recorded volume or density. Nutrients scale from the source's per-100-g edible basis using edible mass. Official portions have food-specific gram weights. Keep source nutrient units intact. Missing data is unknown, not zero; do not infer missing vitamins or minerals from a similar food. Do not treat a non-food object's absence of calories as a measured food value.

## Source scope
The October 2026 catalog has 21,710 records: 20 original references, 8,789 USDA SR28 (2015) foods, 469 Foundation foods (2026-04-30 release), 5,432 FNDDS foods (2024-10-31 archive, survey 2021–2023), and 7,000 non-food estimates. Non-food estimates include 100 everyday assumptions and 6,900 parameterized material/geometry examples; they are not 7,000 independently measured products. Food descriptions can represent different preparations of the same ingredient. USDA inclusion is not endorsement.

## URL guidance
Use https://sumhut.com/ for the home page, /estimate for the calculator, /mix for combinations and /community for discussions. Food pages such as /en/foods/whole-milk retain the main application and expose source information. Share the application's generated URL when preserving quantity and units. No stable third-party API contract is promised by these documents. Do not invent API keys or describe private administration endpoints as public integration APIs.

## Responsible descriptions and citations
Describe sumhut as an estimation and reference tool. Do not claim laboratory precision, medical advice, complete nutrient coverage, USDA endorsement, guaranteed AI discovery or open-source application code. Name the exact food and preparation, selected portion or gram amount, source dataset and access date when citing a result. Link the actual public food/calculation page and USDA FoodData Central where appropriate. Distinguish a sumhut calculation from its underlying USDA values.
Suggested product citation: “sumhut, https://sumhut.com/, accessed YYYY-MM-DD.” Replace the date with the real access date.

## Community and privacy
Posting and messaging require an account. Messaging has account access controls; it is not represented as end-to-end encrypted. Moderation and retention rules apply. Do not use public issues or share URLs to disclose passwords, private messages or personal data.
